questions.question: Explain Java's platform independence.
questions.answer: The Java compiler produces bytecode rather than machine code. A Java Virtual Machine for each operating system executes the same bytecode, giving Java its write once, run anywhere model.

questions.question: Differentiate JDK, JRE and JVM.
questions.answer: The JVM executes bytecode. The JRE contains the JVM and runtime libraries. The JDK contains the JRE plus development tools such as javac, javadoc and debugger utilities.

questions.question: Differentiate String, StringBuffer and StringBuilder.
questions.answer: String is immutable. StringBuffer is mutable and synchronized. StringBuilder is mutable but not synchronized and is usually faster in single-threaded code.

questions.question: Explain method overloading and method overriding.
questions.answer: Overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists and is resolved at compile time. Overriding supplies a subclass implementation with the same signature and supports runtime polymorphism.

questions.question: Differentiate checked and unchecked exceptions.
questions.answer: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared, such as IOException. Unchecked exceptions inherit RuntimeException and need not be declared, such as ArithmeticException.

questions.question: What is thread synchronization and why is it needed?
questions.answer: Synchronization controls concurrent access to shared mutable data. It prevents race conditions by allowing only one thread at a time to execute a protected critical section or method.

questions.question: List the major stages in the Applet life cycle.
questions.answer: init(), start(), paint(), stop() and destroy(). init initializes once; start activates; paint draws; stop pauses; destroy releases resources.

questions.question: What is the event-delegation model?
questions.answer: An event source creates an event object and sends it to registered listener objects. The listener's handler method processes the event, separating component logic from event handling.

questions.question: State the main JDBC steps.
questions.answer: Load/register the driver, obtain a Connection, create a Statement or PreparedStatement, execute SQL, process the ResultSet when present, commit or roll back as required, and close resources.

questions.question: Differentiate Socket and ServerSocket.
questions.answer: A Socket represents one endpoint of a TCP connection and is used by clients and accepted server connections. A ServerSocket listens on a port and accepts incoming client connections.

questions.question: Differentiate GET and POST.
questions.answer: GET sends parameters in the URL and is suited to safe retrieval. POST sends data in the request body and is suited to submissions that may change server state or contain more data.

questions.question: Name four session-tracking techniques.
questions.answer: Cookies, URL rewriting, hidden form fields and HttpSession.

questions.question: Explain Java features, program structure, data types, operators and control statements.
questions.answer: Cover portability, robustness, object orientation, security and multithreading; class and main method structure; primitive/reference types; major operator groups; if/switch and loop statements, with short examples.

questions.question: Explain classes, constructors, inheritance, abstract classes, interfaces and runtime polymorphism with examples.
questions.answer: Define each concept, show constructor chaining with super, access control, overriding through a base reference, an abstract method, and multiple-type inheritance using interfaces.

questions.question: Explain Java exception handling and multithreading in detail.
questions.answer: Discuss try, catch, finally, throw, throws, checked/unchecked exceptions and custom exceptions. Cover thread creation, life cycle, priorities, sleep, join, synchronization and inter-thread communication.

questions.question: Explain the Applet life cycle, AWT controls, layout managers and event handling.
questions.answer: Describe each Applet life-cycle method; Label, Button, TextField, Checkbox and Choice; Flow, Border, Grid and Card layouts; event sources, event objects, listeners and adapters. Note that Applets are legacy technology.

questions.question: Explain JDBC architecture and database access with transactions and connection pooling.
questions.answer: Cover drivers, DriverManager/DataSource, Connection, Statement, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, ResultSet, commit/rollback, resource closing and how a pool lends and reuses connections.

questions.question: Explain Servlet architecture, life cycle, session tracking, JSP elements and tag libraries.
questions.answer: Cover container responsibilities, init/service/destroy, doGet/doPost, request/response, cookies and HttpSession, JSP directives/declarations/scriptlets/expressions, implicit objects and JSTL/custom tags.

questions.question: What does executeUpdate() normally return after an UPDATE statement?
questions.answer: It returns an int containing the number of rows affected by the SQL statement.

questions.question: A Servlet calls request.getSession() twice during one request. Are two sessions created? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The first call returns an existing valid session or creates one; the second call returns the same session associated with that request/client.

questions.question: Write a Java program to test whether an input number is prime.
Create Student and Result classes using inheritance and display total and average marks.
Write a Java program with two threads that print odd and even numbers.
questions.answer:
class Printer implements Runnable { int start; Printer(int s){start=s;} public void run(){for(int i=start;i<=10;i+=2)System.out.print(i+" ");} }
class Main { public static void main(String[] a)throws Exception {Thread odd=new Thread(new Printer(1));Thread even=new Thread(new Printer(2));odd.start();even.start();odd.join();even.join();} }

questions.question: Create an AWT Frame containing a TextField and Button; display a message when the button is clicked.
questions.answer:
import java.awt.*; import java.awt.event.*;
class Demo extends Frame implements ActionListener { TextField t=new TextField(20); Button b=new Button("Show"); Demo(){setLayout(new FlowLayout());add(t);add(b);b.addActionListener(this);setSize(300,150);setVisible(true);} public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e){t.setText("Welcome");} public static void main(String[] x){new Demo();} }
